item.title: Children with additional needs could be denied their rights, Longford protest hears
item.description: Children with additional needs risk being denied their right to equal access to education. That's according to parents and carers who protested in Longford Town over the weekend over the government's review of SNAs. Plans to cut allocations of Special Needs Assistants in over 200 schools across the country were paused for this year after public backlash. item.title: Carrick's €20m sports complex on course to be finished next year
item.description: The €20 million sports complex in Carrick-on-Shannon is set to be completed next year. The Shannonside Recreational Campus is about to go to tender. It will include an athletics track, an AstroTurf pitch, sports arena, and a standard grass pitch. item.title: Local garda numbers have fallen in past decade, new figures reveal
item.description: A new ten-year comparison shows a drop in local Garda numbers covering the Shannonside region in the last ten years. The figures come amid ongoing concerns about resources, recruitment and visibility in rural communities. In 2016, there were 898 serving members across the Sligo-Leitrim and Roscommon-Longford divisions. Advertisement That figure has now fallen to 866 in 2026 - a reduction of 32 gardaí. item.title: Westmeath man jailed for abuse of sister
item.description: A 79-year-old man has been sentenced to three years in prison for the historic abuse of his sister. Seán Monaghan of The Harbour, Marketpoint, Mullingar in Westmeath had pleaded guilty to the rape and indecent assault of Julie Fogarty on dates in 1962 and 1963. At his sentence hearing today, the court heard Ms Fogarty experiences "repeated flashbacks" and " wakes up crying in the night still". item.title: Famine Way to expand to US, Boyle man reveals
item.description: The National Irish Famine Way, which begins in Co Roscommon, is set to expand to the United States this year. It's part of the Global Irish Famine Way project, which aims to install commemorations of the Great Famine around the world. The US Global Irish Famine Way follows the trail in Canada, which was established last year. item.title: Roscommon journalist says situation in Abu Dhabi is 'stable for now'
item.description: A Roscommon man living in Abu Dhabi says he feels safe despite ongoing Iranian rocket attacks. Shane Reynolds, a journalist from Elphin, says the main international airport remains closed due to the ongoing conflict. People have been urged to work from home in the United Arab Emirates capital. Shane's family in Roscommon have pleaded with him to leave the country. Speaking to Dan Dooner, he says there's currently no way out: Advertisement

item.title: Free events for Longford businesses as part of Local Enterprise Week
item.description: Small and medium businesses in Longford can avail of a number of free online and in person workshops this week. It's part of Local Enterprise Week which runs until Friday afternoon. Hundreds of online and in person events are taking place at venues across the country as part of the initiative. Longford's Senior Enterprise Development Officer Catherine Kane says one of the main events is taking place tomorrow: Future-proofing and Women in Business will also feature this week: Advertisement

item.title: IFA ends sit-in protest at Bord Bia HQ after 28 days
item.description: Members of the Irish Farmers Association have ended their sit-in-protest at Bord Bia this evening. The breaking news comes after agreement that a 'governance review' will take place into matters raised by the IFA in recent weeks. Bord Bia's Chair Larry Murrin will remain as chair while the review takes place, but will not chair meetings during the review period.
